title: Juicy British Meat Sunday Roast
description: A traditional British Sunday roast featuring slow-cooked tender meat, crispy crackling, and a hint of yellow curry paste. Perfect for a comforting family dinner.

ingredients.name: Braising pork shoulder
ingredients.notes: Look for a boneless pork shoulder with a good layer of fat.

ingredients.name: Yellow curry paste
ingredients.notes: Use a high-quality curry paste for the best flavor.

ingredients.name: Vegetable oil
ingredients.notes: Use a neutral-tasting oil with a high smoke point.

ingredients.name: Onions
ingredients.notes: Choose sweet onions for the best flavor.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.notes: Use a mix of orange and purple carrots for a pop of color.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.notes: Choose high-starch potatoes for the fluffiest roast potatoes.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Mince the garlic for the best flavor.

ingredients.name: Thyme
ingredients.notes: Use fresh thyme for the best flavor.

ingredients.name: Bay leaves
ingredients.notes: Use fresh or dried bay leaves for the best flavor.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use kosher salt for the best flavor.

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: Use freshly ground black pepper for the best flavor.

ingredients.name: Crispy deep-fry potatoes
ingredients.notes: Use leftover potatoes for a crispy snack.

ingredients.name: Gravy granules
ingredients.notes: Use homemade or store-bought gravy granules for the best flavor.

ingredients.name: Beef broth
ingredients.notes: Use low-sodium beef broth for the best flavor.

instructions: Season the pork shoulder with salt and black pepper, then rub with yellow curry paste.
Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear the pork shoulder until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes per side.
Transfer the pork to a plate and set aside.
Add the remaining 6 tablespoons of vegetable oil to the Dutch oven, then add the sliced onions and cook until caramelized, about 10 minutes.
Add the sliced carrots and cook until tender, about 5 minutes.
Add the sliced potatoes and cook until tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the thyme sprigs and bay leaves to the Dutch oven, then add the beef broth and bring to a boil.
Return the pork shoulder to the Dutch oven and transfer to the preheated oven.
Roast the pork for 2-3 hours, or until tender and falling apart.
Cook pork to an internal temperature of 63°C / 145°F and let it rest for 3 minutes before serving.
